Everything you asked for is now built and on `main` (plus PR #24). Here's the direct answer to your three questions.

## 1. Translate the opus drafts

```bash
# translate work/content_bank_build/PHP/runs/opus/drafts/ with deepseek-v4-flash
uv run python -m content_bank.author.translate_cli --book PHP \
    --drafts-dir work/content_bank_build/PHP/runs/opus/drafts
```
Needs a credential — `ARK_API_KEY` in `.env` for deepseek, or add `--backend claude --model opus` to use your Claude subscription. (Add `--items PHP-001-D1-01 …` to translate just a few first.)

## 2. Where results land

`work/content_bank_build/PHP/runs/opus/translations/<translator-slug>/<item_id>.json` — one **proposal** per item:
```jsonc
{ "id": "...", "en": "...", "item": { "text": {"en": "...", "zh": "…「CUV」…"} },
  "cuv_refs": [...], "gate_ok": true, "gate_flags": [], "drift": {...}, "uncertain": [] }
```
`gate_ok` = CUV/glossary passed; `drift` = back-translation doctrinal check. You review these, then land accepted ones with `translate.promote(...)` (it writes only `zh` into the store, never advancing `review_status`).

## 3. Compare translators

Run the translation again with a different translator, then generate the comparison page:
```bash
# same opus drafts, opus as the translator this time
uv run python -m content_bank.author.translate_cli --book PHP \
    --drafts-dir work/content_bank_build/PHP/runs/opus/drafts \
    --backend claude --model opus

# side-by-side page
uv run python -m content_bank.author.translate_compare_html PHP \
    --draft-run opus --translators deepseek-v4-flash,opus
# → work/content_bank_build/PHP/runs/opus/translations/review.html  (open in a browser)
```
The page shows, per item: **English ▸ CUV source verse ▸ each translator's Chinese ▸ gate/drift/uncertain flags** — so you can see which translator hews to CUV and keeps the doctrine intact. Each translator writes to its own dir, so runs never collide.

"""The single LLM seam for content-bank authoring.

Rendered prompt in, completion text out. This is the swappable/mockable ``llm()``
seam issue #16's standalone builder (``build_cli.py``) calls after
``build_brief_prompt.build(...)`` and ``build_draft_prompt.build(...)``.

Two backends, selected by ``SCRIPTURE_LOOM_LLM_BACKEND`` (default ``llm_core``):

- ``llm_core`` — the vendored synchronous mxlens path (default model
  deepseek-v4-flash, billed to API credits). Cheap and fast; the quality ceiling
  is the model.
- ``claude`` — shells out to the Claude Code CLI in headless print mode
  (``claude -p``), billing against the logged-in **subscription** (no
  ``ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`` in the environment ⇒ the CLI uses the OAuth login). Gets a
  strong model (default ``opus``) at no marginal per-token cost, at the price of
  per-call process spawn + subscription usage windows.

Both are pure "prompt in, text out" and raise ``RuntimeError`` on failure, so the
builder's backoff + per-unit isolation handle either identically.
"""
import os
import subprocess

# Built-in tools disabled for a pure single-shot completion (the prompts are
# fully self-contained; the model must not shell out or read files). NOTE: do
# NOT add ``--bare`` — it skips the credential source and breaks subscription
# auth ("Not logged in").
_CLAUDE_NO_TOOLS = ["Bash", "Read", "Edit", "Write", "Glob", "Grep",
                    "WebFetch", "WebSearch", "Task", "NotebookEdit"]
_CLAUDE_TIMEOUT_S = 900


def llm(prompt: str, model: str | None = None) -> str:
    """Send one fully-rendered prompt, return the completion text.

    Backend from ``SCRIPTURE_LOOM_LLM_BACKEND`` (``llm_core`` default, or
    ``claude``). ``model`` defaults to ``SCRIPTURE_LOOM_LLM_MODEL`` if set, else
    the backend's own default (deepseek-v4-flash / opus). Raises ``RuntimeError``
    on failure.
    """
    if model is None:
        model = os.environ.get("SCRIPTURE_LOOM_LLM_MODEL") or None
    if os.environ.get("SCRIPTURE_LOOM_LLM_BACKEND") == "claude":
        return _claude_cli_llm(prompt, model)
    from llm_core import run_sync_llm

    return run_sync_llm("", prompt, caller="content_bank", model=model)


def _claude_cli_llm(prompt: str, model: str | None = None) -> str:
    """One headless Claude Code completion via ``claude -p`` (subscription auth).

    Prompt goes on stdin (so it never collides with the variadic tool flags).
    """
    argv = ["claude", "-p", "--model", model or "opus",
            "--output-format", "text",
            "--disallowed-tools", *_CLAUDE_NO_TOOLS]
    proc = subprocess.run(argv, input=prompt, capture_output=True, text=True,
                          timeout=_CLAUDE_TIMEOUT_S)
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"claude -p failed (exit {proc.returncode}): {proc.stderr[:500]}")
    out = (proc.stdout or "").strip()
    if not out:
        raise RuntimeError("claude -p returned empty output")
    return out

    """One synchronous completion via the SHARED LLM path (`LLMService.
    run_batch_sync`) — the same OpenAI-format, usage-tracked core that backs the
    run_llm_batch task / POST /api/v1/llm/batch. Raises on unconfigured/unknown
    model or after bounded retry; callers (SOFT sites) catch and degrade
    fail-open."""
    if not llm_configured():
        raise RuntimeError(
            "analyst in-recipe LLM not configured (set llm_api_key/llm_api_base "
            "or a provider key like ARK_API_KEY); SOFT sites degrade fail-open")

    from llm_core.service import LLMService

    resolved = model or settings.analyst_llm_model
    # Proper OpenAI messages (system + user turns), not a concatenated blob.
    messages = ([{"role": "system", "content": system_prompt}] if system_prompt else []) \
        + [{"role": "user", "content": user_message}]
    # Endpoint override for a self-hosted / non-default endpoint; when unset the
    # model self-configures its provider endpoint + key from the environment.
    build_overrides = _build_overrides()

    last_err = "empty"
    for attempt in range(1, _MAX_ATTEMPTS + 1):
        t0 = time.time()
        try:
            out = LLMService.run_batch_sync(
                [messages], model=resolved, build_overrides=build_overrides,
                cache=settings.analyst_llm_cache_enabled)
        except ValueError as exc:  # unbuildable model — not transient
            raise RuntimeError(f"analyst LLM: unknown model {resolved!r}: {exc}") from exc
        gen = out["generations"][0]
        summary = out["summary"]
        elapsed = int((time.time() - t0) * 1000)
        if not gen.get("error") and gen.get("generation"):
            _log.info("analyst.llm.ok", caller=caller, model=resolved, attempt=attempt,
                      elapsed_ms=elapsed, tokens_out=summary.get("tokens_out_total"),
                      cost=summary.get("cost"))
            return gen["generation"]
        last_err = gen.get("error") or "empty"
        _log.warning("analyst.llm.retry", caller=caller, model=resolved,
                     attempt=attempt, elapsed_ms=elapsed, error=str(last_err)[:200])
    raise RuntimeError(
        f"analyst LLM failed after {_MAX_ATTEMPTS} attempts "
        f"(caller={caller}, model={resolved}): {last_err}")


def _build_overrides() -> dict:
    o = {}
    if settings.llm_api_base:
        o["api_base"] = settings.llm_api_base
    if settings.llm_api_key:
        o["api_key"] = settings.llm_api_key
    return o

## The mechanism

`reasoning_effort` isn't a per-call argument in this stack — it's baked into the **model menu entry**. So I added a new key `deepseek-v4-flash-medium` in `llm_core/chatmodels/menu.py` that reuses the same flash ARK endpoint (`deepseek-v4-flash-260425`) but with `reasoning_effort: "medium"`. Because the run slug is derived from the model key, this gives you **both** things at once: medium reasoning **and** a distinct output id (`deepseek-v4-flash-medium` ≠ `deepseek-v4-flash`).

Per-item failures are logged\n    and skipped, matching the previous sequential behaviour.\n    \"\"\"\n    results = [None] * len(items)\n    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(\n            max_workers=max(1, concurrency)) as ex:\n        futs = {ex.submit(proposal_for, it, book, glossary=glossary,\n                          model=model, max_repair=max_repair): i\n                for i, it in enumerate(items)}\n        for fut in concurrent.futures.as_completed(futs):\n            i = futs[fut]\n            it = items[i]\n            try:\n                p = fut.result()\n            except Exception as exc:  # isolate per item\n                print(f\"[FAIL] {it['id']}: {exc}\")\n                continue\n            results[i] = p\n            print(f\"[ok] {it['id']}\" + (\"\" if p[\"gate_ok\"] else \" (gate flags)\")\n                  + (\" (drift)\" if p[\"drift\"][\"drift\"] else \"\"))\n    return [p for p in results if p is not None]\n\n\ndef write_proposals(proposals, out_dir):"
}
```

### 🤖 Assistant · 2026-07-22T01:03:31.808Z

Both fixes are done and the full suite passes (250 OK).

## What changed

**1. Answer & notes now show up — it was a display gap, not a translation gap.**

The translations *were* being produced all along: `leader_reference.text.zh` (the answer key / leader note) and `verse.zh` are in every proposal JSON. But `translate_compare_html.py` only rendered `item.text.zh`, so the reviewer never saw them. I extended the comparison page to render, under each item's main text:
- **Answer:** / **Notes:** — the translated `leader_reference.text` (labelled by kind: `answer_key`→Answer, `leader_note`→Notes)
- **Verse:** — the translated `leader_reference.verse`
- the English source of both, in the English column

Regenerating the existing PHP page confirms it: 109 `Answer:`, 72 `Notes:`, 109 `Verse:` blocks now appear.

**2. Translation is now parallel across items.**

`translate_cli.main` ran items in a plain `for` loop — each item waiting on the previous one's full translate→repair→back-translate LLM chain. I added `run_proposals(...)`, a `ThreadPoolExecutor` fan-out (each item's own chain stays sequential, but N items are in flight at once). The LLM seam is I/O-bound — both the llm_core network call and the `claude -p` subprocess release the GIL while waiting — so threads give real speed-up. New `--concurrency` flag, default 4. Per-item failure isolation and `[ok]`/`[FAIL]` logging are preserved; results stay in input order.

```bash
uv run python -m content_bank.author.translate_cli --book PHP \
    --drafts-dir work/content_bank_build/PHP/runs/opus/drafts \
    --model deepseek-v4-flash --concurrency 8
```

At concurrency 8, a 74-item run should be roughly 8× faster (bounded by the provider's own rate limits).

Tests added: `run_proposals` order-preservation + failure-isolation; leader_reference carried into the page and rendered (answer, verse, en source). Changes are unstaged on `main` — say the word if you'd like me to branch and commit, and whether to bump the default concurrency higher than 4.

One adjacent gap I noticed but did **not** touch (you asked only about answer/notes): `category` on `pre_reading_quest` items is a bilingual field that `_merge_zh` and the prompt schema don't handle, so `category.zh` is never produced. Want me to fold that into the translator too?

7	这三个目标有时会冲突，因此最好采用“先翻译、再改写、最后审校”的流程，而不是一次生成最终译文。
8	
9	## 一、先定义“初学者易懂”的具体标准
10	
11	可以在系统提示词中明确规定：
12	
13	* 面向第一次系统学习圣经的青少年或成年人
14	* 使用现代、自然的书面中文
15	* 一个句子尽量只表达一个主要思想
16	* 避免连续使用多个抽象神学名词
17	* 较长英文句子拆成两到三个中文句子
18	* 少用“乃是、故此、藉此、于其中、其所”等较旧的书面表达
19	* 不假设读者已经理解教会术语
20	* 术语第一次出现时，用一句简短解释
21	* 不把严肃内容改成幼儿化或网络化语言
22	* 不随意增加原文没有的神学判断
23	
24	这里最重要的是：
25	
26	> **易懂不等于删除神学术语，而是保留术语，同时帮助读者理解。**
27	
28	例如：
29	
30	* 不建议把 justification 只翻译成“上帝认为我们是好人”
31	* 更合适的是：“称义，就是神因着基督宣告罪人为义。”
32	
33	## 二、建立受控的神学术语表
34	
35	Bible study guide 很容易出现术语前后不一致的问题。应当给 LLM 提供一个项目级 glossary。
36	
37	例如：
38	
39	| 英文             | 固定译法  | 面向初学者的解释          |
40	| -------------- | ----- | ----------------- |
41	| justification  | 称义    | 神因着基督宣告罪人为义       |
42	| sanctification | 成圣    | 圣灵逐渐改变信徒，使人越来越像基督 |
43	| atonement      | 赎罪    | 基督担当罪的刑罚，使人与神和好   |
44	| covenant       | 约     | 神主动设立、带有应许和要求的关系  |
45	| repentance     | 悔改    | 离开罪，转向神           |
46	| grace          | 恩典    | 神白白赐给不配之人的恩惠      |
47	| righteousness  | 义／公义  | 根据上下文选择，不要机械统一    |
48	| flesh          | 肉体／罪性 | 必须根据经文语境判断        |
49	
50	术语表最好不仅记录“怎么翻”，还记录：
51	
52	* 哪些词不能简化
53	* 哪些词必须根据上下文选择
54	* 第一次出现时如何解释
55	* 哪些译法符合你的神学传统
56	* 哪些译法需要避免
57	
58	例如，`flesh` 不能每次都翻成“肉体”，因为保罗书信中有时指人的罪性倾向，而不是身体本身。
59	
60	## 三、使用三阶段翻译流程
61	
62	### 第一阶段：忠实翻译
63	
64	这一阶段只关心含义、逻辑和术语准确，不急着追求特别流畅。
65	
66	要求模型输出：
67	
68	* 基本译文
69	* 关键术语
70	* 可能存在歧义的句子
71	* 原文中的逻辑关系
72	
73	### 第二阶段：初学者改写
74	
75	让模型在不改变含义的前提下：
76	
77	* 拆分长句
78	* 补全中文中必要的主语
79	* 将抽象表达改成具体表达
80	* 调整英文式语序
81	* 给首次出现的术语加简短解释
82	* 把问题改成自然的中文提问方式
83	
84	### 第三阶段：忠实度审校
85	
86	最后再让模型对照英文检查：
87	
88	* 是否遗漏限定词
89	* 是否把“可能”翻成“必然”
90	* 是否把描述翻成命令
91	* 是否增加原文没有的因果关系
92	* 是否弱化罪、审判、悔改、救赎等概念
93	* 是否把作者的解释误写成经文本身的话
94	* 神学术语是否与 glossary 一致
95	
96	这种流程比“一次翻译完成”可靠得多。
97	
98	## 四、建议保留两个中文版本
99	
100	在内部数据结构中，可以同时保留：
101	
102	```json
103	{
104	  "faithful_translation": "忠实、接近原文结构的译文",
105	  "reader_friendly_translation": "适合初学者阅读的最终版本",
106	  "term_notes": [
107	    {
108	      "term": "justification",
109	      "translation": "称义",
110	      "explanation": "神因着基督宣告罪人为义"
111	    }
112	  ],
113	  "uncertainties": []
114	}
115	```
116	
117	面向用户只显示 `reader_friendly_translation`，但编辑人员可以查看忠实版本和术语说明。
118	
119	这样，流畅性改写就不会覆盖掉原始翻译依据。
120	
121	## 五、给不同内容类型制定不同规则
122	
123	Bible study guide 不是一种单一文本。不同内容应采用不同翻译方式。
124	
125	### 经文引用
126	
127	不要让 LLM 自己翻译已有中文圣经经文。
128	
129	应当：
130	
131	* 保存经文引用位置
132	* 使用指定中文圣经版本替换
133	* 明确标注版本
134	* 让 LLM 只翻译经文周围的讲解
135	
136	否则会出现“看起来像圣经，但实际上是模型自译”的内容。
137	
138	### 背景介绍
139	
140	可以采用较自然的说明文风格：
141	
142	> 保罗写这封信时，罗马教会中既有犹太信徒，也有外邦信徒。由于他们的背景不同，在饮食、节期和律法等问题上常有不同看法。
143	
144	不要机械地保留英文名词化结构：
145	
146	> 在罗马教会中存在犹太人与外邦人之间关于饮食实践的张力。
147	
148	后一句虽然准确，但不适合初学者。
149	
150	### 观察题
151	
152	尽量使用能从经文直接找到答案的表达：
153	
154	* “这段经文重复了哪个词？”
155	* “耶稣在这里吩咐门徒做什么？”
156	* “第6节怎样描述这个人？”
157	
158	避免：
159	
160	* “请识别该文本中的重复性词汇。”
161	* “作者在此采用了怎样的修辞策略？”
162	
163	### 解释题
164	
165	先问经文在说什么，再问原因：
166	
167	* “这里的‘光’指什么？”
168	* “为什么作者把信徒称为‘光明之子’？”
169	
170	### 应用题
171	
172	避免模糊、宽泛或容易制造属灵压力的问题：
173	
174	不太好：
175	
176	> 你是否真正把生命完全交给了神？
177	
178	更具体：
179	
180	> 这段经文指出了哪一种需要离开的行为？本周你可以采取什么具体行动？
181	
182	## 六、让模型遵循“保留术语，解释术语”的原则
183	
184	可以使用三种处理方式。
185	
186	### 直接保留
187	
188	适用于已经比较常见的词：
189	
190	> 福音、罪、恩典、悔改、信心、复活。
191	
192	### 保留并解释
193	
194	适用于重要但初学者可能不熟悉的词：
195	
196	> “称义”是指神因着基督宣告罪人为义。
197	
198	### 使用普通表达后标出术语
199	
200	适用于第一次介绍某个概念：
201	
202	> 神使信徒逐渐改变，越来越像基督。这个过程通常称为“成圣”。
203	
204	第三种方式通常对初学者最友好。
205	
206	## 七、提供明确的风格提示词
207	
208	可以把下面这段作为翻译系统提示词的基础。
209	
210	```text
211	你是一位圣经学习材料的中文编辑。你的任务不是逐字直译，
212	而是在忠实保留原文含义、逻辑关系和神学术语的前提下，
213	生成适合圣经初学者阅读的自然中文。
214	
215	目标读者：
216	- 第一次系统学习圣经的青少年或成年人
217	- 具备普通中文阅读能力
218	- 不一定熟悉教会和神学术语
219	
220	翻译要求：
221	1. 使用现代、自然、清楚的简体中文。
222	2. 一个句子尽量只表达一个主要思想。
223	3. 英文长句可以拆分，但不可删除逻辑关系和限定条件。
224	4. 避免生硬的英文语序和过度名词化的表达。
225	5. 保留重要的圣经和神学术语。
226	6. 术语第一次出现时，用简短、准确的一句话解释。
227	7. 不要为了容易理解而弱化罪、审判、悔改、信心、
228	   恩典、救赎和基督工作的含义。
229	8. 不增加原文没有的解释、例子或应用。
230	9. 区分经文所说的话、作者的解释和学习材料提出的问题。
231	10. 经文引用不得自行重译，应保留引用标记，等待系统替换为指定版本。
232	11. 避免使用幼儿化、网络化或过于随意的表达。
233	12. 使用项目提供的术语表，并保持前后一致。
234	
235	输出前检查：
236	- 初学者是否能在第一次阅读时理解句子的主语和主要意思？
237	- 是否存在可以拆开的长句？
238	- 是否有未解释的专业术语？
239	- 是否改变了原文的程度、条件、因果或语气？
240	```
241	
242	## 八、增加一个专门的“中文编辑器”角色
243	
244	翻译模型经常产生“没有错误，但不像中文”的句子。因此可以在翻译后增加一个独立提示：
245	
246	```text
247	请把下面的译文作为中文编辑进行润色。
248	
249	不要查看英文原文，也不要重新解释内容。
250	只处理中文表达问题：
251	
252	- 修正英文式语序
253	- 拆分过长句子
254	- 补全不清楚的主语
255	- 删除不必要的重复
256	- 把抽象名词结构改成自然的动词表达
257	- 保留所有神学术语、限定条件和逻辑关系
258	- 不增加新的解释或应用
259	- 使文字适合圣经初学者朗读和讨论
260	```
261	
262	让这个步骤暂时不看英文，有一个好处：它会真正从中文读者的角度判断流畅性，而不是不断受到英文句式影响。
263	
264	之后再用第三阶段对照英文审校。
265	
266	## 九、用对比例子训练或提示模型
267	
268	英文原文：
269	
270	> Paul reminds believers that Christian freedom should not become an excuse for self-centered living, but should express itself through loving service to others.
271	
272	生硬译文：
273	
274	> 保罗提醒信徒，基督徒的自由不应该成为以自我为中心的生活的借口，而应该通过对他人的爱心服事来表达它自己。
275	
276	适合初学者的译文：
277	
278	> 保罗提醒信徒：基督徒虽然得了自由，却不能以此为借口，只顾满足自己。真正的自由应当表现为凭着爱心彼此服事。
279	
280	改进点包括：
281	
282	* 删除“表达它自己”这种英文式表达
283	* 把长句拆开
284	* 将 `self-centered living` 具体化为“只顾满足自己”
285	* 保留“自由—爱心服事”的逻辑对比
286	* 没有添加原文之外的神学内容
287	
288	## 十、建立可自动执行的质量评分
289	
290	可以让另一个模型按四个维度评分，每项1—5分：
291	
292	| 维度     | 检查内容            |
293	| ------ | --------------- |
294	| 忠实度    | 是否保留原文含义、条件和逻辑  |
295	| 神学准确性  | 术语和教义表述是否准确     |
296	| 中文流畅性  | 是否像自然中文，而不是英文句式 |
297	| 初学者可读性 | 是否需要已有神学知识才能读懂  |
298	
299	同时设置硬性错误：
300	
301	* 经文引用被自行改写
302	* 核心术语译错
303	* 删除否定词或限定词
304	* 原文的“可能”被翻成“必然”
305	* 原文问题被改成断言
306	* 增加原文没有的属灵应用
307	* 把作者的观点说成“圣经明确教导”
308	
309	发现硬性错误时，无论流畅性评分多高，都应退回重译。
310	
311	## 十一、最适合实际产品的流程
312	
313	推荐采用下面的管线：
314	
315	```text
316	英文原文
317	   ↓
318	内容分类
319	   ├─ 经文引用 → 从授权中文圣经中替换
320	   ├─ 背景说明
321	   ├─ 观察题
322	   ├─ 解释题
323	   └─ 应用题
324	   ↓
325	术语识别与 glossary 注入
326	   ↓
327	忠实翻译
328	   ↓
329	初学者中文改写
330	   ↓
331	中文流畅性编辑
332	   ↓
333	英文对照审校
334	   ↓
335	规则检查与评分
336	   ↓
337	最终译文
338	```
339	
340	最核心的设计原则可以概括为：
341	
342	> **先固定含义，再改善中文；保留神学术语，但降低理解术语所需要的门槛。**
343	
344	不要让模型同时自由决定“原文是什么意思、术语怎么翻、初学者需要知道什么、中文怎样更自然”。将这些决策拆开，翻译的稳定性和可控性会明显提高。
345	
```

I'll use the **brainstorming** skill for this — you're asking a "how to achieve" design question, and the hints doc is essentially a spec proposal. Let me map it against what we already have, then settle the key decision before designing.

## Where the current pipeline already meets the hints

Our per-item flow today is: `build_translate_prompt` (one prompt carrying BSB/CUV pairs + glossary + WCF‑1 frame + rules + structured output) → single `translate` call → `cuv_quote_check`/`glossary_check` **repair loop** → `back_translate_review` **drift check**.

So we already implement, in compressed form:
- **§三 stage 1 (faithful) + §三 stage 3 (fidelity review)** — the prompt demands faithful meaning; `back_translate_review` is the English-comparison audit.
- **§五 经文引用** — this is the whole point of the CUV-alignment gate: the model never self-translates Scripture; it substitutes verbatim CUV in 「」, enforced by `cuv_quote_check`.
- **§二 glossary pinning** — `glossary.json` + `glossary_check`, with `avoid` renderings flagged.

## The real gaps (what the doc adds)

1. **Fluency and beginner-rewrite are collapsed into the faithful prompt.** The doc's core claim (§三, §八) is that asking one call to *simultaneously* decide meaning, terms, beginner-needs, and natural Chinese produces "correct but not-like-Chinese" prose. It wants a **separate Chinese-editor pass that doesn't look at the English** (§八).
2. **Glossary has no beginner explanation / first-use gloss** (§二, §六) — our entries are `en_term → zh_term` only; the doc wants a "保留并解释" explanation and first-occurrence gloss injection.
3. **No content-type-specific style** (§五) — observation vs interpretation vs application questions want different phrasing; we have `type`/`dimension` but the prompt ignores them.
4. **No 4-dimension score gate** (§十) — faithfulness / theology / fluency / readability, with hard-error rollback.
5. **No dual-version retention** (§四) — `faithful_translation` vs `reader_friendly_translation`.

## The tension I need you to resolve first

The doc's full pipeline is **3–5 LLM calls per item**. You *just* asked me to cut latency (the concurrency work). A dedicated fluency-editor pass alone would roughly double calls; the full pipeline with scoring triples-to-quintuples them. So the pivotal design choice is how deep to go.

### 🤖 Assistant · 2026-07-22T20:38:22.121Z

Here's my honest critique of the hints doc — where it's right, where it's wrong for *this* project, and where it's fighting itself.

## What the doc gets genuinely right

- **§五 "don't let the model translate Scripture" is the single most important point, and we already do exactly this.** This is the doc's best insight, and it's load-bearing. Our CUV-alignment gate *is* this principle mechanized. If the doc had said nothing else, it would still be worth reading.
- **§三/§八 "separate meaning-fixing from Chinese-polishing" is real.** The observation that one prompt juggling meaning + terms + beginner-needs + naturalness produces "correct but not-like-Chinese" prose is true and matches how LLMs actually fail. This is the strongest *new* idea for us.
- **§二 glossary with beginner explanations** is a cheap, high-value add that doesn't cost extra calls.

## Where I'd push back hard

**1. The doc optimizes for quality as if latency and cost were free. They aren't — you told me so an hour ago.** The full §十一 pipeline is 5+ sequential calls per item, and stages 2→3→4 are *strictly serial* (each needs the prior output), so concurrency across items helps but the per-item wall-clock triples. A book is ~250 items. That's the direct opposite of what you just paid me to fix. The doc never once weighs this. **I don't trust a design that ignores the constraint the user cares most about.**

**2. §四 "keep two Chinese versions" is over-engineering for your product.** Scripture Loom ships *one* reader-facing zh. The faithful version would exist only for an editor who — realistically — will read the English source anyway (it's right there in the compare page). You'd pay a schema migration, gate changes, promote changes, and page columns for an artifact almost nobody opens. **YAGNI.** The *drift review* already gives editors the "did fluency soften the meaning?" signal without storing a second string.

**3. §八 "fluency editor must NOT see the English" is half-right and half-dangerous.** The upside (judge Chinese as Chinese) is real. But a blind editor is exactly the step that can smooth "may abound" into "必然丰盛," drop a limiting clause, or round a question into an assertion — the doc's *own* §十 hard-error list. The doc's answer is "then re-audit against English afterward," which means you deliberately introduce drift and then hope to catch it. **For a text where theology rigidity is a hard requirement, a pass that's structurally blind to the source is a risk, not a feature.** The mitigation has to be mechanical, not another LLM opinion: after the fluency pass, re-run `cuv_quote_check` (CUV spans must survive verbatim) and `glossary_check` (mandated terms must survive) — *those* are deterministic and can't be sweet-talked. The blind-editor idea only earns its place if it's bracketed by hard gates.

**4. §十 "let another model score 1–5 on four dimensions" is the weakest section.** LLM self-scoring is noisy, gameable, and gives false confidence — a 4/5 "faithfulness" score is not evidence of faithfulness. The *useful* half of §十 is the **hard-error list** (Scripture rewritten, term wrong, negation dropped, "may"→"must", question→assertion, added application). Those are checkable — some already are (`cuv_quote_check`, `glossary_check`), and the rest are better as targeted deterministic checks or a single focused adversarial prompt than as a soft rubric. **Keep the hard-error gate; drop the numeric scoring theater.**

**5. §六 first-use term explanation collides with your item model.** The doc assumes flowing prose where "称义" appears once and gets a parenthetical gloss. But your content is *atomized items* — a D1 drill, a separate D6 application question — with no guaranteed reading order and no "first occurrence." Injecting "（称义就是…）" into every item that mentions it is clutter; injecting it into none defeats the purpose. **First-use gloss is a document-level concept applied to a non-document data model.** It needs rethinking (maybe glossary explanations live in the *leader_reference*, not the reader text), not literal transcription.

## The one structural thing the doc is right about that we lack

**Content-type-aware phrasing (§五).** This is the cheapest real win and it fits our model perfectly, because every item *already carries* `type` and `dimension`. An observation question (D1–D2) should read "这段经文重复了哪个词？"; an application question (D8) should be concrete, not "你是否真正把生命交给神？". Right now the prompt treats all items identically. We can inject per-type/per-dimension style guidance with **zero extra calls** — it's just prompt text keyed off fields we have.

## My bottom line before we design

The doc is a good *checklist of failure modes* and a poor *pipeline blueprint for your constraints*. I'd take:

- **In:** one fluency-editor pass **bracketed by the existing hard gates** (§八 done safely), content-type style rules (§五, free), glossary explanations surfaced to *editors* not readers (§二/§六 adapted).
- **Out:** dual-version storage (§四), numeric self-scoring (§十), literal first-use gloss in reader text (§六), and the naive 5-stage serial pipeline (§十一).

That lands almost exactly on my "Recommended" earlier: **~2 calls/item, single zh, gates re-run after the polish.** The difference now is you know *why* I'm rejecting the rest of the doc rather than just picking the cheap option.

Want me to now turn that into a concrete design (spec), or do you want to argue me back toward any of the pieces I cut?

## The one correction: tags don't remove string matching — they move it from *discovery* to *verification*

Right now `quote_detect.py` does **discovery**: it scans the prose for maximal spans that happen to appear verbatim in BSB, and *guesses* which ref each belongs to. That's heuristic — it can mis-bound a span or misattribute a ref.

Your tag doesn't let the gate skip comparison. The `ref` is a **model claim**, not a fact — if the gate trusted it blind, the model could wrap any text in `<bible_verse ref='PHP.1.6'>` and assert it's Scripture. So the gate still compares `tagged_text == corpus[ref]`. What changes is that the comparison becomes **exact and unambiguous** — boundaries and ref are given, so it's a one-shot equality check instead of a fuzzy search. That *is* a real, worthwhile win (precision goes to 100%, attribution is explicit), just not "no matching." Keep that framing straight or the gate gets built to trust the tag, which would *weaken* rigidity.

## The load-bearing distinction: two tag *modes*, not one

Scripture and the Standards need different verification, and conflating them is the trap:

- `<verse ref='PHP.1.6'>…</verse>` → **quote mode**: the inner text MUST equal the corpus verbatim (BSB for en, CUV for zh). Deterministically *verifiable*.
- `<wcf ref='1.4'>…</wcf>` (and WLC/WSC) → **basis mode**: the content *references* a doctrine, it doesn't quote the confession. You cannot verify the paraphrase verbatim. What the gate CAN check deterministically is that the ref **resolves to a real section** — the claim *names a basis*. Whether the claim is *faithful* to that section stays a human/adversarial judgment.

So one tag vocabulary, two semantics — maybe `<verse>` vs `<doctrine ref=… standard="WCF|WLC|WSC">`, or a `mode="quote|basis"` attribute. `text.en` / `text.zh` is what prints on the paper kit — you can't ship `<verse>` markup to families. So decide the source-of-truth:

- **Store the tagged string as canonical; strip tags at render; gates read the markup.** Single source of truth, edit-stable. Cost: `validate.py`, the store, and the prototype renderer/selector all must strip. This is my recommendation.

Both good questions — they're really about *function vs. overlap* and *separation of powers*. Clear opinions on each.

## 1. Short phrase quotes — tag by *function*, not by length

The question isn't "how many words" — it's **"is this presented as a quotation, or is it the author's own prose that happens to reuse a biblical word?"** Two different things:

- *"He calls them "the light of the world.""* — a 4-word quote, functioning as a quotation → **tag it.**
- *"Paul writes about the good work God is doing"* — "good work" overlaps `PHP.1.6` but is woven into the author's sentence, not quoted → **don't tag.** Forcing verbatim CUV on incidental word-overlap would wreck ZH fluency for zero fidelity gain (and this is exactly why your §三 "widen to the smallest contiguous CUV span" rule exists).

So the rule: **anything the author marks as a quote (quotation marks / 「」, or the `verse`/`memory_verse` fields) gets a tag regardless of how short — down to a floor; unmarked incidental overlap does not.** Keep the existing 4-word / 4-han floor, but only as a **false-positive guard for the detector cross-check** — the authoritative signal is "the author marked it as a quotation," which the tag makes explicit.

One mechanical consequence worth noting now: for a **sub-verse phrase**, quote-mode verification is *containment*, not equality — the tagged text must be a contiguous verbatim substring of `corpus[ref]` (normalized). Full-verse and `memory_verse` tags check equality. Same gate, two comparison modes depending on span length. And the en tag and zh tag for the same `ref` needn't be equal-length — the zh may be widened to a CUV clause — because the `ref` links them and each side is checked against its own corpus version.

## 2. The LLM creates the tags. The script only verifies them.

This one I feel strongly about — **authorship stays with the model; the gate is an independent auditor.**

- **Only the model knows *intent*.** Which words it *means* as a quotation vs. its own prose is exactly the thing a script can't know — a script can only detect overlap, which drops you right back into the heuristic-discovery ambiguity we're trying to escape. If the script writes the tags, you've rebuilt `quote_detect`'s guessing and called it a gate.
- **Basis-mode tags are impossible for a script.** No script can infer which WCF/WLC/WSC section a doctrinal claim rests on. Only the model (or human) knows the basis. So doctrine tags *must* be model-authored — there's no alternative.
- **Separation of powers is the whole point of the gate.** A script that both writes and checks its own tags is grading its own work — no independent adversary. The architecture's spine is "AI proposes, deterministic gate disposes"; self-authored gates collapse that.

The script's job is the *other* half:

| Actor | Job |
|---|---|
| **LLM** | Emits tags — quote-mode (`<verse ref>`) and basis-mode (`<doctrine ref standard>`) — as part of structured generation/translation. |
| **Gate (script)** | (a) verifies each quote-mode tag against `corpus[ref]` (equality or containment); (b) verifies each basis-mode ref *resolves* to a real section; (c) runs `quote_detect` as a **recall cross-check** — an untagged verbatim span is a "you missed a tag" *flag*; (d) fails **closed** on malformed tags. |

Note (c) is a *flag for repair* — the model re-tags — **not** an auto-insert. If the detector finds an untagged verbatim overlap, only the model can confirm whether it's a real quotation or coincidental word-reuse (your Q1 case). Auto-inserting would reintroduce the misattribution problem and quietly break fluency. So even the recall net hands authority back to the model.

# Design: Semi-structured citation tags + two-mode hard gate (foundation)

## 1. Scope (this spec only)
The load-bearing, cross-cutting change: a tag vocabulary, the schema/render decision, and the two-mode gate. **Explicitly out** (follow-on specs that build on this): EN content-type style rules, the ZH fluency-editor pass, editor-facing glossary explanations.

## 2. Tag vocabulary
Two inline elements, canonical corpus ref format, minimal attributes:

- **Scripture (quote mode):** `<verse ref="PHP.1.6">that He who began a good work in you…</verse>`
  - `ref` matches `REF_RE` / range form (`PHP.1.1-11`).
- **Standards (basis mode):** `<doctrine std="WCF" ref="1.4">…the claim…</doctrine>`
  - `std ∈ {WCF, WLC, WSC}`; `ref` is chapter.section for WCF (`1.4`), question id for WSC/WLC (`Q1`).

Inline (not a sidecar list) so quote position within the sentence is preserved.

## 3. Canonical storage & rendering
- **The tagged string is the source of truth** in `text` / `leader_reference.text` / `leader_reference.verse` (and their `zh`).
- **Render strips tags, keeps inner text.** One regex strip, applied at every reader-facing surface: the prototype kit renderer, and the compare pages. Nothing with markup ever reaches a family.
- Rejected alternative: clean text + char-offset sidecar (offsets drift on any edit).

## 4. The gate (`citation_check`, deterministic)
Per item, per language:
- **quote-mode:** inner text must be a verbatim, normalized match of `corpus[ref]` for the right version (**BSB** for en, **CUV** for zh) — *equality* for full-verse/`memory_verse`, *containment* (contiguous substring) for a sub-verse phrase.
- **basis-mode:** `ref` must **resolve** to a real section of `std`. Faithfulness of the paraphrase stays a human/adversarial judgment — the gate only guarantees a basis is *named and real*.
- **recall net:** run `quote_detect` after; an untagged verbatim BSB/CUV span is a "missed tag" **flag for repair** (model re-tags) — never auto-inserted.
- **fail-closed:** malformed/unclosed/unknown tags or unresolvable refs = gate failure → repair loop (the existing `_repair_to_clean` / `translate_with_gates` machinery).

## 5. Authorship & flow (ties the two pipelines together)
- **LLM authors all tags; the gate only verifies** — authorship never moves to a script (that would rebuild heuristic discovery).
- **EN generation:** model emits `<verse>` + `<doctrine>` tags; gate verifies verse text vs **BSB** and that doctrine refs resolve.
- **ZH translation:** tags are **carried through**; model translates inner text, re-tags the zh Scripture span as verbatim **CUV** (widening per your §三 rule), and the blind fluency pass is told **"never alter text inside a tag"** — verified byte-identical afterward. No new `<doctrine>` minted.

## 6. Prompt changes
`build_draft_prompt` and `build_translate_prompt` gain a tagging section: tag-by-function (marked quotations only, down to the 4-word/4-han floor), canonical ref format, the two elements, "translate inner text but keep Scripture spans verbatim CUV."

## 7. Backward compatibility
Untagged legacy content (existing PHP/MAT drafts) stays valid: no tags ⇒ nothing to verify by tag, but the `quote_detect` recall net still flags untagged quotes on the next authoring/translate pass. Migration = re-tag on next touch; no bulk rewrite required.

## 8. Testing
Network-free, mocked `llm`: gate accepts a correct `<verse>`, rejects altered inner text, accepts a sub-verse containment match, rejects an out-of-range/malformed tag, resolves/rejects `<doctrine>` refs, flags an untagged verbatim span, and the render-strip produces clean reader text. TDD per the plan.

2. Small naming call: `<verse>`/`<doctrine>` with `ref`/`std` — good, or do you want shorter tags (`<v>`/`<d>`) to cut token overhead and model error?

On your yes, I'll write it to `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-23-citation-tags-foundation-design.md`, commit, and then move to the implementation plan.

It does **not** mint\n  new `<doctrine>` tags — a doctrinal claim originates in English; translation\n  only renders it. Prompt changes\n\n- `build_draft_prompt.py`: add a \"Citation tagging\" section — the two\n  elements, canonical ref format, \"tag every quoted verse and every claim that\n  rests on WCF/WLC/WSC; tag by function, down to the 4-word floor; do not tag\n  incidental word overlap.\"\n- `build_translate_prompt.py`: add \"preserve every tag; translate inner text;\n  keep Scripture spans verbatim CUV inside `<verse>`; copy `<doctrine>`\n  `std`/`ref` unchanged and translate only the inner paraphrase.\"\n\n### 6. Backward compatibility & migration\n\n- **Untagged legacy content stays valid.** An item with no tags has nothing to\n  verify by tag; `citation_check` passes it on the tag checks. The\n  `quote_detect` recall net still flags any untagged verbatim quote in it, so\n  legacy items with quotes surface as `citation.untagged_quote` on their next\n  authoring/translate touch.\n- **Migration is lazy:** re-tag on next touch. No bulk rewrite of PHP/MAT.\n- `store_writer` / schema validation: the tagged string is still a non-empty\n  string, so no schema change is required for storage. Tag *well-formedness*\n  is enforced by the gate, not by schema validation.\n\n## Testing\n\nNetwork-free, `llm` mocked. New `content_bank/tests/test_citation_check.py`\nand `test_standards.py`:\n\n- accepts a correct `<verse>` (equality, full verse);\n- accepts a sub-verse `<verse>` by containment;\n- rejects a `<verse>` whose inner text was altered (`verse_mismatch`);\n- rejects an out-of-range / malformed `ref` and unbalanced tags\n  (`malformed`, fail-closed);\n- `<doctrine std=\"WCF\" ref=\"1.4\">` resolves; `ref=\"1.99\"` and `std=\"XYZ\"`\n  do not (`basis_unresolved`);\n- `WSC`/`WLC` `Q1` resolves; `Q999` does not;\n- an untagged verbatim BSB span is flagged `untagged_quote`;\n- `strip_tags` yields clean reader text for both elements and leaves untagged\n  text unchanged;\n- CUV path: a `zh` `<verse>` verifies against CUV-simp.\n\nRender-strip is covered where the renderers are tested\n(`test_translate_compare_html.py`, prototype/compare tests).\n\n## File-level impact (for the plan)\n\n- **New:** `content_bank/lib/standards.py`, tests.\n- **Modify:** `content_bank/author/gates.py` (add `citation_check`, register in\n  `run_all`), `build_draft_prompt.py`, `build_translate_prompt.py`,\n  `compare_html.py` + `translate_compare_html.py` (strip on render), the\n  prototype kit renderer (strip on render), `translate.py` (carry tags).\n- **Reuse unchanged:** `quote_detect.py`, `corpus_bridge.passage_text`, the\n  existing repair loops.\n"
}

24	def pericope_ids(book):
25	    return {p["id"] for p in pericopes(book)}

28	def book_name(book, lang="en"):
29	    books = _load("canon/structure/books.json")
30	    key = "name_zh" if lang == "zh" else "name_en"
31	    return books[book][key]
32	
33	
34	def wcf_chapter1_text():
35	    wcf = _load("canon/lampposts/wcf.json")
36	    ch1 = next(c for c in wcf["chapters"] if c["n"] == 1)
37	    lines = [f"Chapter 1: {ch1['title']}"]
38	    for s in ch1["sections"]:
39	        lines.append(f"1.{s['n']} {s['text']}")
40	    return "\n".join(lines)
41

43	def passage_text(range_str, version="BSB"):
44	    import sys
45	    corpus_dir = str(_CORPUS)
46	    if corpus_dir not in sys.path:
47	        sys.path.insert(0, corpus_dir)
48	    from lib import passage  # corpus/lib/passage.py
49	    p = passage.get_passage(version, range_str, mode="product")
50	    # Serve verses in canonical (chapter, verse) order — get_passage's dict is
51	    # string-keyed, so "MAT.4.10" sorts before "MAT.4.2" unless we sort numerically.
52	    verses = sorted(p.verses.items(), key=lambda kv: _parse_range(kv[0])[1:3])
53	    return "\n".join(f"{ref}  {text}" for ref, text in verses)
54	
55	
56	def _parse_range(range_str):
57	    """'MAT.5.3-12' or 'MAT.5.3' -> ('MAT', 5, 3, 12)."""
58	    book, chapter, verses = range_str.split(".", 2)
59	    v1, v2 = (verses.split("-", 1) if "-" in verses else (verses, verses))
60	    return book, int(chapter), int(v1), int(v2)
61	
62	
63	def _overlaps(a, b):
64	    return a[0] == b[0] and a[1] == b[1] and a[2] <= b[3] and b[2] <= a[3]
65	
66	
67	def _safe_overlaps(target, ref):
68	    try:
69	        return _overlaps(target, _parse_range(ref))
70	    except (ValueError, AttributeError):
71	        return False
72	
73	
74	def commentary(range_str, book="MAT", works=("mhc", "jfb")):
75	    target = _parse_range(range_str)
76	    out = {}
77	    for work in works:
78	        data = _load(f"canon/lampposts/{work}/{book.lower()}.json")
79	        blocks = data.get("blocks", []) if isinstance(data, dict) else []
80	        out[work] = [b for b in blocks if _safe_overlaps(target, b["range"])]
81	    return out
82	
83	
84	def crossrefs(range_str, limit=15):
85	    target = _parse_range(range_str)
86	    data = _load("canon/structure/crossrefs.json")
87	    refs = data.get("refs", []) if isinstance(data, dict) else data
88	    hits = [r for r in refs if _safe_overlaps(target, r["from"])]
89	    hits.sort(key=lambda r: (-r.get("weight", 0), r.get("to", "")))
90	    return hits[:limit]
91	
92	
93	def section_ids(book):
94	    """Section ids declared in the corpus section map, or empty if none."""
95	    try:
96	        from corpus.lib import sections as _sections
97	        return {s["id"] for s in _sections.load(book)["sections"]}
98	    except FileNotFoundError:
99	        return set()
100	
101	
102	def confessional_refs(range_str):
103	    target = _parse_range(range_str)
104	
105	    def _via(proof_texts):
106	        for pt in proof_texts:
107	            if _safe_overlaps(target, pt):
108	                return pt
109	        return None
110	
111	    out = {"wcf": [], "wlc": [], "wsc": []}
112	    wcf = _load("canon/lampposts/wcf.json")
113	    for ch in wcf["chapters"]:
114	        for s in ch["sections"]:
115	            via = _via(s.get("proof_texts", []))
116	            if via:
117	                out["wcf"].append({"ref": f"WCF {ch['n']}.{s['n']}",
118	                                   "title": ch["title"], "text": s["text"], "via": via})
119	    for key, fname in (("wlc", "wlc.json"), ("wsc", "wsc.json")):
120	        cat = _load(f"canon/lampposts/{fname}")
121	        for q in cat["questions"]:
122	            via = _via(q.get("proof_texts", []))
123	            if via:
124	                out[key].append({"ref": f"{key.upper()} Q{q['n']}",
125	                                 "q": q["q"], "a": q["a"], "via": via})
126	    return out
127

4	of the item's own passage + any structured ref it cites — independent of

11	DETECT_MIN_WORDS = 4
12	
13	
14	def _detect_ranges(item):
15	    ranges = []
16	    if item.get("passage"):
17	        ranges.append(item["passage"])
18	    for tok in gates._stated_refs(item):
19	        if tok not in ranges:

22	
23	
24	def _english_strings(item):
25	    out = []

27	    if isinstance(t.get("en"), str):
28	        out.append(t["en"])
29	    ref = item.get("leader_reference") or {}
30	    for key in ("text", "verse"):
31	        m = ref.get(key) or {}
32	        if isinstance(m.get("en"), str):
33	            out.append(m["en"])
34	    return out
35	
36	
37	def _haystacks(item):
38	    hays = []
39	    for r in _detect_ranges(item):
40	        try:
41	            text = corpus_bridge.passage_text(r, version="BSB")
42	        except Exception:
43	            continue
44	        hays.append((r, gates._norm(text)))
45	    return hays
46	
47	
48	def detect_quotes(item, book):
49	    hays = _haystacks(item)
50	    found = []
51	    for s in _english_strings(item):
52	        words = s.split()
53	        n = len(words)
54	        i = 0
55	        while i < n:
56	            best_j, best_ref = i, None
57	            j = i + 1
58	            while j <= n:
59	                phrase = gates._norm(" ".join(words[i:j]))
60	                match = next((ref for ref, h in hays if phrase and phrase in h), None)
61	                if match is None:
62	                    break
63	                best_j, best_ref = j, match
64	                j += 1
65	            if best_j - i >= DETECT_MIN_WORDS:
66	                found.append({"quote": " ".join(words[i:best_j]), "ref": best_ref})
67	                i = best_j
68	            else:
69	                i += 1
70	    return found

75	def _repair_prompt(item, flags):
76	    return ("Your Chinese translation has these problems — fix ONLY them, keeping "
77	            "everything else identical, and return the SAME strict JSON shape:\n"
78	            + "\n".join(f"- {f}" for f in flags)
79	            + "\n\n## Current item (with your zh)\n"

85	def translate_with_gates(item, book, *, glossary=None, model=None, max_repair=2):
86	    glossary = _glossary.load_glossary() if glossary is None else glossary
87	    out = translate_item(item, book, glossary=glossary, model=model)
88	    flags = zh_gate_flags(out["item"], glossary)
89	    rounds = 0
90	    while flags and rounds < max_repair:
91	        rounds += 1
92	        resp = _extract_json(llm(_repair_prompt(out["item"], flags), model))
93	        out["item"] = _merge_zh(out["item"], resp)
94	        if "terms" in resp:
95	            out["terms"] = resp["terms"]
96	        if "uncertain" in resp:
97	            out["uncertain"] = resp["uncertain"]
98	        flags = zh_gate_flags(out["item"], glossary)
99	    out["gate_ok"] = not flags
100	    out["gate_flags"] = flags
101	    return out

104	def back_translate_review(item, *, model=None):
105	    zh = " ".join(s for l, s in gates._lang_strings(item) if l == "zh")
106	    en = " ".join(s for l, s in gates._lang_strings(item) if l == "en")
107	    if not zh.strip():
108	        return {"drift": False, "notes": "no zh"}
109	    prompt = (
110	        "Back-translate the Chinese below into English, then compare its DOCTRINAL "
111	        "meaning to the original English and the Westminster frame. Flag any drift: "
112	        "softened/strengthened/added/removed doctrine, or judgment stated as fact.\n\n"
113	        f"## Original English\n{en}\n\n## Chinese to check\n{zh}\n\n"
114	        f"## Westminster frame\n{corpus_bridge.wcf_chapter1_text()}\n\n"
115	        'Return STRICT JSON ONLY: {"drift": true|false, "notes": "concrete"}.')
116	    v = _extract_json(llm(prompt, model))
117	    return {"drift": bool(v.get("drift")), "notes": v.get("notes", "")}

120	def _merge_zh_into_store_item(store_item, proposal_item):
121	    """Copy ONLY zh text values from the proposal onto the store item."""
122	    out = copy.deepcopy(store_item)
123	    p_text = (proposal_item.get("text") or {})
124	    if "zh" in p_text:
125	        out.setdefault("text", {})["zh"] = p_text["zh"]
126	    p_lr = proposal_item.get("leader_reference") or {}
127	    o_lr = out.get("leader_reference")
128	    if isinstance(o_lr, dict):
129	        if "zh" in (p_lr.get("text") or {}):
130	            o_lr.setdefault("text", {})["zh"] = p_lr["text"]["zh"]
131	        if isinstance(o_lr.get("verse"), dict) and "zh" in (p_lr.get("verse") or {}):
132	            o_lr["verse"]["zh"] = p_lr["verse"]["zh"]
133	    if isinstance(out.get("category"), dict) and "zh" in (proposal_item.get("category") or {}):
134	        out["category"]["zh"] = proposal_item["category"]["zh"]
135	    return out
136	
137	
138	def promote(book, proposals, accepted_ids, *, store_dir=None):
139	    accepted = set(accepted_ids)
140	    store = content.load_book_store(book, store_dir)
141	    by_id = {it["id"]: it for it in store["items"]}
142	    to_write, promoted = [], []
143	    for p in proposals:
144	        if p["id"] not in accepted:
145	            continue
146	        if p["id"] not in by_id:
147	            raise KeyError(f"{p['id']} not in {book} store")
148	        to_write.append(_merge_zh_into_store_item(by_id[p["id"]], p["item"]))
149	        promoted.append(p["id"])
150	    if to_write:
151	        store_writer.upsert_items(book, to_write, store_dir)
152	    return promoted

10	def display_ref(range_str, lang="en"):
11	    # range_str like "MAT.5.3-12" or "MAT.5.1" (single verse)
12	    book_code, chapter, verses = range_str.split(".", 2)
13	    name = corpus_bridge.book_name(book_code, lang)
14	    if "-" in verses:
15	        v1, v2 = verses.split("-", 1)

17	    else:

22	def load_bank(book, lang="en", store_dir=None):
23	    pericopes = [
24	        {
25	            "id": p["id"],
26	            "ref": display_ref(p["range"], lang),
27	            "title": p.get("title_zh") if lang == "zh" and p.get("title_zh") else p["title_en"],
28	        }
29	        for p in corpus_bridge.pericopes(book)
30	    ]
31	    items = []
32	    for it in content.get_content(book, lang=lang, mode="product", store_dir=store_dir):
33	        flat = {k: v for k, v in it.items() if k not in ("text", "category")}
34	        flat["body"] = it["text"][lang]
35	        if "category" in it and lang in it["category"]:
36	            flat["category"] = it["category"][lang]
37	        items.append(flat)
38	    return {"pericopes": pericopes, "items": items}
39	
40	
41	def load_sections(book, lang="en"):
42	    """Flattened section list for the selector: title[lang] -> 'title'."""
43	    from corpus.lib import sections as sections_lib
44	    out = []
45	    for s in sections_lib.load(book)["sections"]:
46	        title = s.get("title_zh") if lang == "zh" and s.get("title_zh") else s["title_en"]
47	        out.append({
48	            "id": s["id"], "title": title,
49	            "first_pericope": s["first_pericope"],
50	            "last_pericope": s["last_pericope"],
51	            "marker": s.get("marker"),
52	        })
53	    return out

Unknown `std`, malformed `ref`, or out-of-range number → `None`.\n\nCanon shapes (verified): `wcf.json` → `{\"chapters\": [{\"n\": int, \"sections\": [{\"n\": int, \"text\": str}]}]}`; `wlc.json`/`wsc.json` → `{\"questions\": [{\"n\": int, \"q\": str, \"a\": str}]}`.\n\n- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**\n\n```python\n# content_bank/tests/test_standards.py\nimport unittest\nfrom content_bank.lib import standards\n\n\nclass TestResolve(unittest.TestCase):\n    def test_wcf_section_resolves(self):\n        text = standards.resolve(\"WCF\", \"1.4\")\n        self.assertIsInstance(text, str)\n        self.assertIn(\"authority\", text.lower())\n\n    def test_wcf_out_of_range_is_none(self):\n        self.assertIsNone(standards.resolve(\"WCF\", \"1.99\"))\n        self.assertIsNone(standards.resolve(\"WCF\", \"99.1\"))\n\n    def test_wcf_bad_ref_shape_is_none(self):\n        self.assertIsNone(standards.resolve(\"WCF\", \"Q1\"))\n        self.assertIsNone(standards.resolve(\"WCF\", \"1\"))\n\n    def test_wsc_and_wlc_question_resolves(self):\n        self.assertIn(\"glorify\", standards.resolve(\"WSC\", \"Q1\").lower())\n        self.assertIsInstance(standards.resolve(\"WLC\", \"Q1\"), str)\n\n    def test_question_out_of_range_is_none(self):\n        self.assertIsNone(standards.resolve(\"WSC\", \"Q9999\"))\n        self.assertIsNone(standards.resolve(\"WSC\", \"1.4\"))\n\n    def test_unknown_standard_is_none(self):\n        self.assertIsNone(standards.resolve(\"XYZ\", \"1.1\"))\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    unittest.main()\n```\n\n- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**\n\nRun: `uv run python -m unittest content_bank.tests.test_standards -v`\nExpected: FAIL — `ModuleNotFoundError: content_bank.lib.standards`.\n\n- [ ] **Step 3: Write minimal implementation**\n\n```python\n# content_bank/lib/standards.py\n\"\"\"Resolve a Westminster Standards citation against the committed canon\nlampposts. WCF ref is \"chapter.section\"; WLC/WSC ref is \"Q<number>\".\nReturns the cited text if it exists, else None. Network-free.\"\"\"\nimport re\n\nfrom . import corpus_bridge\n\n_FILES = {\"WCF\": \"canon/lampposts/wcf.json\",\n          \"WLC\": \"canon/lampposts/wlc.json\",\n          \"WSC\": \"canon/lampposts/wsc.json\"}\n_WCF_RE = re.compile(r\"^(\\d+)\\.(\\d+)$\")\n_Q_RE = re.compile(r\"^Q(\\d+)$\")\n\n\ndef resolve(std, ref):\n    if std not in _FILES:\n        return None\n    data = corpus_bridge._load(_FILES[std])\n    if std == \"WCF\":\n        m = _WCF_RE.match(ref or \"\")\n        if not m:\n            return None\n        c, sec = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2))\n        ch = next((x for x in data[\"chapters\"] if x[\"n\"] == c), None)\n        if ch is None:\n            return None\n        s = next((x for x in ch[\"sections\"] if x[\"n\"] == sec), None)\n        return s[\"text\"] if s else None\n    m = _Q_RE.match(ref or \"\")\n    if not m:\n        return None\n    n = int(m.group(1))\n    q = next((x for x in data[\"questions\"] if x[\"n\"] == n), None)\n    return q[\"a\"] if q else None\n```\n\n- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**\n\nRun: `uv run python -m unittest content_bank.tests.test_standards -v`\nExpected: PASS.\n\n- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**\n\n```bash\ngit add content_bank/lib/standards.py content_bank/tests/test_standards.py\ngit commit -m \"feat(standards): resolve WCF/WLC/WSC citations vs canon lampposts\"\n```\n\n---\n\n### Task 3: `citation_check` gate + registration in `run_all`\n\n**Files:**\n- Modify: `content_bank/author/gates.py`\n- Test: `content_bank/tests/test_citation_check.py`\n\n**Interfaces:**\n- Consumes: `citation_tags.parse`, `standards.resolve`, `corpus_bridge.passage_text`, `quote_detect.detect_quotes` (lazy import to avoid the `gates`↔`quote_detect` cycle), and the existing `_lang_strings`, `_norm`, `_EN_VERSION`, `_ZH_VERSION`.\n- Produces: `citation_check(items, *, langs=None) -> {id: [flags]}`. `langs` filters which language strings are checked (`None` = all). import pathlib
import sys
import unittest

sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))
from content_bank.lib import prototype_bank as pb


class TestDisplayRef(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_multi_verse(self):
        self.assertEqual(pb.display_ref("MAT.5.3-12", "en"), "Matthew 5:3–12")

    def test_two_verse(self):
        self.assertEqual(pb.display_ref("MAT.5.1-2", "en"), "Matthew 5:1–2")

    def test_cross_chapter_style_range(self):
        self.assertEqual(pb.display_ref("MAT.4.1-11", "en"), "Matthew 4:1–11")


class TestLoadBank(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.bank = pb.load_bank("MAT", lang="en")

    def test_pericopes_include_corpus_ids_with_display_refs(self):
        by_id = {p["id"]: p for p in self.bank["pericopes"]}
        self.assertEqual(by_id["MAT-014"]["ref"], "Matthew 5:3–12")
        self.assertEqual(by_id["MAT-014"]["title"], "The Beatitudes")

    def test_items_flattened_to_body_and_product_gated(self):
        # load_bank serves product mode (published only), flattening text/category
        # for the requested language to a 'body' string; no reviewed/draft leaks.
        self.assertTrue(self.bank["items"])
        item = self.bank["items"][0]
        self.assertIsInstance(item["body"], str)
        self.assertNotIn("text", item)
        statuses = {i.get("review_status") for i in self.bank["items"]}
        self.assertNotIn("draft", statuses)
        self.assertNotIn("reviewed", statuses)

    def test_load_sections_flattens_titles(self):
        from content_bank.lib import prototype_bank
        secs = prototype_bank.load_sections("MAT", lang="en")
        self.assertEqual(len(secs), 7)
        self.assertEqual(secs[0]["id"], "MAT-S1")
        self.assertEqual(secs[0]["title"], "Prologue: The Infancy")
        self.assertEqual(secs[0]["first_pericope"], "MAT-001")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

Base directory for this skill: /home/pb/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/superpowers/6.1.1/skills/subagent-driven-development

# Subagent-Driven Development

Execute plan by dispatching a fresh implementer subagent per task, a task review (spec compliance + code quality) after each, and a broad whole-branch review at the end.

**Why subagents:** You delegate tasks to specialized agents with isolated context. By precisely crafting their instructions and context, you ensure they stay focused and succeed at their task. They should never inherit your session's context or history — you construct exactly what they need. This also preserves your own context for coordination work.

**Core principle:** Fresh subagent per task + task review (spec + quality) + broad final review = high quality, fast iteration

**Narration:** between tool calls, narrate at most one short line — the
ledger and the tool results carry the record.

**Continuous execution:** Do not pause to check in with your human partner between tasks. Execute all tasks from the plan without stopping. The only reasons to stop are: BLOCKED status you cannot resolve, ambiguity that genuinely prevents progress, or all tasks complete. "Should I continue?" prompts and progress summaries waste their time — they asked you to execute the plan, so execute it.

## When to Use

```dot

    "Have implementation plan?" [shape=diamond];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" [shape=diamond];
    "Stay in this session?" [shape=diamond];
    "subagent-driven-development" [shape=box];

    "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [shape=box];

    "Have implementation plan?" -> "Tasks mostly independent?" [label="yes"];
    "Have implementation plan?" -> "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [label="no"];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" -> "Stay in this session?" [label="yes"];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" -> "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [label="no - tightly coupled"];
    "Stay in this session?" -> "subagent-driven-development" [label="yes"];
    "Stay in this session?" -> "executing-plans" [label="no - parallel session"];
}
```

**vs. Executing Plans (parallel session):**
- Same session (no context switch)
- Fresh subagent per task (no context pollution)
- Review after each task (spec compliance + code quality), broad review at the end
- Faster iteration (no human-in-loop between tasks)

    "Mark task complete in todo list and progress ledger" -> "More tasks remain?";
    "More tasks remain?" -> "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)" [label="yes"];
    "More tasks remain?" -> "Dispatch final code reviewer subagent (../requesting-code-review/code-reviewer.md)" [label="no"];
    "Dispatch final code reviewer subagent (../requesting-code-review/code-reviewer.md)" -> "Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch";
}
```

## Pre-Flight Plan Review

Before dispatching Task 1, scan the plan once for conflicts:

- tasks that contradict each other or the plan's Global Constraints
- anything the plan explicitly mandates that the review rubric treats as a
  defect (a test that asserts nothing, verbatim duplication of a logic block)

Present everything you find to your human partner as one batched question —
each finding beside the plan text that mandates it, asking which governs —
before execution begins, not one interrupt per discovery mid-plan. If the
scan is clean, proceed without comment. The review loop remains the net for
conflicts that only emerge from implementation.

## Model Selection

Use the least powerful model that can handle each role to conserve cost and increase speed.

**Mechanical implementation tasks** (isolated functions, clear specs, 1-2 files): use a fast, cheap model. Most implementation tasks are mechanical when the plan is well-specified.

**Integration and judgment tasks** (multi-file coordination, pattern matching, debugging): use a standard model.

**Architecture and design tasks**: use the most capable available model.
The final whole-branch review is one of these — dispatch it on the most
capable available model, not the session default.

**Review tasks**: choose the model with the same judgment, scaled to the
diff's size, complexity, and risk. A small mechanical diff does not need the
most capable model; a subtle concurrency change does.

**Always specify the model explicitly when dispatching a subagent.** An
omitted model inherits your session's model — often the most capable and
most expensive — which silently defeats this section.

**Turn count beats token price.** Wall-clock and context cost scale with how
many turns a subagent takes, and the cheapest models routinely take 2-3× the
turns on multi-step work — costing more overall. Use a mid-tier model as the
floor for reviewers and for implementers working from prose descriptions.
When the task's plan text contains the complete code to write, the
implementation is transcription plus testing: use the cheapest tier for
that implementer. Single-file mechanical fixes also take the cheapest tier.

**Task complexity signals (implementation tasks):**
- Touches 1-2 files with a complete spec → cheap model
- Touches multiple files with integration concerns → standard model
- Requires design judgment or broad codebase understanding → most capable model

## Handling Implementer Status

Implementer subagents report one of four statuses. Handle each appropriately:

**DONE:** Generate the review package (`scripts/review-package BASE HEAD`, from this skill's directory — it prints the unique file path it wrote; BASE is the commit you recorded before dispatching the implementer — never `HEAD~1`, which silently drops all but the last commit of a multi-commit task), then dispatch the task reviewer with the printed path.

**DONE_WITH_CONCERNS:** The implementer completed the work but flagged doubts. Read the concerns before proceeding. If the concerns are about correctness or scope, address them before review. If they're observations (e.g., "this file is getting large"), note them and proceed to review.

**NEEDS_CONTEXT:** The implementer needs information that wasn't provided. Provide the missing context and re-dispatch.

**BLOCKED:** The implementer cannot complete the task. Assess the blocker:
1. If it's a context problem, provide more context and re-dispatch with the same model
2. If the task requires more reasoning, re-dispatch with a more capable model
3. If the task is too large, break it into smaller pieces
4. If the plan itself is wrong, escalate to the human

**Never** ignore an escalation or force the same model to retry without changes. If the implementer said it's stuck, something needs to change.

## Handling Reviewer ⚠️ Items

The task reviewer may report "⚠️ Cannot verify from diff" items — requirements
that live in unchanged code or span tasks. These do not block the rest of the
review, but you must resolve each one yourself before marking the task
complete: you hold the plan and cross-task context the reviewer
lacks. If you confirm an item is a real gap, treat it as a failed spec
review — send it back to the implementer and re-review.

## Constructing Reviewer Prompts

Per-task reviews are task-scoped gates. The broad review happens once, at the
final whole-branch review. When you fill a reviewer template:

- Do not add open-ended directives like "check all uses" or "run race tests
  if useful" without a concrete, task-specific reason
- Do not ask a reviewer to re-run tests the implementer already ran on the
  same code — the implementer's report carries the test evidence
- Do not pre-judge findings for the reviewer — never instruct a reviewer to
  ignore or not flag a specific issue. If you believe a finding would be a
  false positive, let the reviewer raise it and adjudicate it in the review
  loop. If the prompt you are writing contains "do not flag," "don't treat X
  as a defect," "at most Minor," or "the plan chose" — stop: you are
  pre-judging, usually to spare yourself a review loop.
- The global-constraints block you hand the reviewer is its attention
  lens. Copy the binding requirements verbatim from the plan's Global
  Constraints section or the spec: exact values, exact formats, and the
  stated relationships between components ("same layout as X", "matches
  Y"). The reviewer's template already carries the process rules (YAGNI,
  test hygiene, review method) — the constraints block is for what THIS
  project's spec demands.
- Hand the reviewer its diff as a file: run this skill's
  `scripts/review-package BASE HEAD` and pass the reviewer the file path
  it prints (or, without bash: `git log --oneline`, `git diff --stat`,
  and `git diff -U10` for the range, redirected to one uniquely named
  file). The output never enters your own context, and the reviewer sees
  the commit list, stat summary, and full diff with context in one Read
  call. Use the BASE you recorded before dispatching the implementer —
  never `HEAD~1`, which silently truncates multi-commit tasks.
- A dispatch prompt describes one task, not the session's history. Do not
  paste accumulated prior-task summaries ("state after Tasks 1-3") into
  later dispatches — a real session's dispatch hit 42k chars of which 99%
  was pasted history. A fresh subagent needs its task, the interfaces it
  touches, and the global constraints. Nothing else.
- Dispatch fix subagents for Critical and Important findings. Record Minor
  findings in the progress ledger as you go, and point the final
  whole-branch review at that list so it can triage which must be fixed
  before merge. A roll-up nobody reads is a silent discard.
- A finding labeled plan-mandated — or any finding that conflicts with
  what the plan's text requires — is the human's decision, like any plan
  contradiction: present the finding and the plan text, ask which governs.
  Do not dismiss the finding because the plan mandates it, and do not
  dispatch a fix that contradicts the plan without asking.
- The final whole-branch review gets a package too: run
  `scripts/review-package MERGE_BASE HEAD` (MERGE_BASE = the commit the
  branch started from, e.g. `git merge-base main HEAD`) and include the
  printed path in the final review dispatch, so the final reviewer reads
  one file instead of re-deriving the branch diff with git commands.
- Every fix dispatch carries the implementer contract: the fix subagent
  re-runs the tests covering its change and reports the results. Name the
  covering test files in the dispatch — a one-line fix does not need the
  whole suite. Before re-dispatching the reviewer, confirm the fix report
  contains the covering tests, the command run, and the output; dispatch
  the re-review once all three are present.
- If the final whole-branch review returns findings, dispatch ONE fix
  subagent with the complete findings list — not one fixer per finding.
  Per-finding fixers each rebuild context and re-run suites; a real
  session's final-review fix wave cost more than all its tasks combined.

## File Handoffs

Everything you paste into a dispatch prompt — and everything a subagent
prints back — stays resident in your context for the rest of the session
and is re-read on every later turn. Hand artifacts over as files:

- **Task brief:** before dispatching an implementer, run this skill's
  `scripts/task-brief PLAN_FILE N` — it extracts the task's full text to a
  uniquely named file and prints the path. Compose the dispatch so the
  brief stays the single source of requirements. Your dispatch should
  contain: (1) one line on where this task fits in the project; (2) the
  brief path, introduced as "read this first — it is your requirements,
  with the exact values to use verbatim"; (3) interfaces and decisions
  from earlier tasks that the brief cannot know; (4) your resolution of
  any ambiguity you noticed in the brief; (5) the report-file path and
  report contract. Exact values (numbers, magic strings, signatures, test
  cases) appear only in the brief.
- **Report file:** name the implementer's report file after the brief
  (brief `…/task-N-brief.md` → report `…/task-N-report.md`) and put it in
  the dispatch prompt. The implementer writes the full report there and
  returns only status, commits, a one-line test summary, and concerns.
- **Reviewer inputs:** the task reviewer gets three paths — the same brief
  file, the report file, and the review package — plus the global
  constraints that bind the task.
- Fix dispatches append their fix report (with test results) to the same
  report file and return a short summary; re-reviews read the updated file.

## Durable Progress

Conversation memory does not survive compaction. In real sessions,
controllers that lost their place have re-dispatched entire completed task
sequences — the single most expensive failure observed. Track progress in
a ledger file, not only in todos.

- At skill start, check for a ledger:
  `cat "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/.superpowers/sdd/progress.md"`. Tasks listed there
  as complete are DONE — do not re-dispatch them; resume at the first task
  not marked complete.
- When a task's review comes back clean, append one line to the ledger in
  the same message as your other bookkeeping:
  `Task N: complete (commits <base7>..<head7>, review clean)`.
- The ledger is your recovery map: the commits it names exist in git even
  when your context no longer remembers creating them. After compaction,
  trust the ledger and `git log` over your own recollection.
- `git clean -fdx` will destroy the ledger (it's git-ignored scratch); if
  that happens, recover from `git log`.

## Prompt Templates

- [implementer-prompt.md](implementer-prompt.md) - Dispatch implementer subagent
- [task-reviewer-prompt.md](task-reviewer-prompt.md) - Dispatch task reviewer subagent (spec compliance + code quality)
- Final whole-branch review: use superpowers:requesting-code-review's [code-reviewer.md](../requesting-code-review/code-reviewer.md)

## Example Workflow

```
You: I'm using Subagent-Driven Development to execute this plan.

[Read plan file once: docs/superpowers/plans/feature-plan.md]
[Create todos for all tasks]

Task 1: Hook installation script

[Run task-brief for Task 1; dispatch implementer with brief + report paths + context]

Implementer: "Before I begin - should the hook be installed at user or system level?"

You: "User level (~/.config/superpowers/hooks/)"

Implementer: "Got it. Implementing now..."
[Later] Implementer:
  - Implemented install-hook command
  - Added tests, 5/5 passing
  - Self-review: Found I missed --force flag, added it
  - Committed

[Run review-package, dispatch task reviewer with the printed path]
Task reviewer: Spec ✅ - all requirements met, nothing extra.
  Strengths: Good test coverage, clean. Issues: None. Task quality: Approved.

[Mark Task 1 complete]

Task 2: Recovery modes

[Run task-brief for Task 2; dispatch implementer with brief + report paths + context]

Implementer: [No questions, proceeds]
Implementer:
  - Added verify/repair modes
  - 8/8 tests passing
  - Self-review: All good
  - Committed

[Run review-package, dispatch task reviewer with the printed path]
Task reviewer: Spec ❌:
  - Missing: Progress reporting (spec says "report every 100 items")
  - Extra: Added --json flag (not requested)
  Issues (Important): Magic number (100)

[Dispatch fix subagent with all findings]
Fixer: Removed --json flag, added progress reporting, extracted PROGRESS_INTERVAL constant

[Task reviewer reviews again]
Task reviewer: Spec ✅. Task quality: Approved.

[Mark Task 2 complete]

...

[After all tasks]
[Dispatch final code-reviewer]
Final reviewer: All requirements met, ready to merge

Done!
```

## Advantages

**vs. Manual execution:**
- Subagents follow TDD naturally
- Fresh context per task (no confusion)
- Parallel-safe (subagents don't interfere)
- Subagent can ask questions (before AND during work)

**vs. Executing Plans:**
- Same session (no handoff)
- Continuous progress (no waiting)
- Review checkpoints automatic

**Efficiency gains:**
- Controller curates exactly what context is needed; bulk artifacts move
  as files, not pasted text
- Subagent gets complete information upfront
- Questions surfaced before work begins (not after)

**Quality gates:**
- Self-review catches issues before handoff
- Task review carries two verdicts: spec compliance and code quality
- Review loops ensure fixes actually work
- Spec compliance prevents over/under-building
- Code quality ensures implementation is well-built

**Cost:**
- More subagent invocations (implementer + reviewer per task)
- Controller does more prep work (extracting all tasks upfront)
- Review loops add iterations
- But catches issues early (cheaper than debugging later)

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Start implementation on main/master branch without explicit user consent
- Skip task review, or accept a report missing either verdict (spec compliance AND task quality are both required)
- Proceed with unfixed issues
- Dispatch multiple implementation subagents in parallel (conflicts)
- Make a subagent read the whole plan file (hand it its task brief —
  `scripts/task-brief` — instead)
- Skip scene-setting context (subagent needs to understand where task fits)
- Ignore subagent questions (answer before letting them proceed)
- Accept "close enough" on spec compliance (reviewer found spec issues = not done)
- Skip review loops (reviewer found issues = implementer fixes = review again)
- Let implementer self-review replace actual review (both are needed)
- Tell a reviewer what not to flag, or pre-rate a finding's severity in the
  dispatch prompt ("treat it as Minor at most") — the plan's example code is
  a starting point, not evidence that its weaknesses were chosen
- Dispatch a task reviewer without a diff file — generate it first
  (`scripts/review-package BASE HEAD`) and name the printed path in the
  prompt
- Move to next task while the review has open Critical/Important issues
- Re-dispatch a task the progress ledger already marks complete — check
  the ledger (and `git log`) after any compaction or resume

**If subagent asks questions:**
- Answer clearly and completely
- Provide additional context if needed
- Don't rush them into implementation

**If reviewer finds issues:**
- Implementer (same subagent) fixes them
- Reviewer reviews again
- Repeat until approved
- Don't skip the re-review

**If subagent fails task:**
- Dispatch fix subagent with specific instructions
- Don't try to fix manually (context pollution)

## Spec Compliance: ✅

The implementation matches `task-1-brief.md` requirements: `Verse`/`Doctrine` namedtuples with the specified fields, `strip_tags` removing all `<verse>`/`<doctrine>` open/close markers while preserving inner text and passing non-strings through unchanged, and `parse` returning `(verses, doctrines, malformed)` with fail-closed malformed detection. Stdlib-only (`re`, `collections.namedtuple`), no corpus imports, no I/O — network-free and deterministic. All 8 tests specified in the brief were implemented verbatim and reported passing.

## Strengths

- Malformed detection is a clean, correct heuristic: it compares the count of raw open/close markers (`_V_OPEN`/`_V_CLOSE`/`_D_OPEN`/`_D_CLOSE`, which match any occurrence of the tag name regardless of well-formedness) against the count of tags that successfully parsed via the strict `_VERSE_RE`/`_DOCTRINE_RE`. Any marker that exists but didn't produce a clean match (missing attribute, wrong quoting, extra attribute, unbalanced open/close) surfaces as a count mismatch → `malformed=True`. This is a good design: it doesn't need special-case logic per failure mode.
- `strip_tags` uses a separate, deliberately loose regex (`_ANY_TAG_RE`) that strips tags regardless of well-formedness, which is the right behavior for a display-time stripper (don't leave broken markup visible even if `parse` would flag it malformed).
- Traced the three specifically-requested angles against the regexes by hand and all hold:
  - **(a) missing closing tag** — `<verse ref="PHP.1.1">servants` has no `</verse>`, so `_VERSE_RE` fails to match (`verses=[]`), but `_V_OPEN` still counts 1 → `1 != 0` → malformed. Correct.
  - **(b) `<verse>` with no `ref`** — `_VERSE_RE` requires `\s+ref="..."` right after `<verse`, so `<verse>` doesn't match (`verses=[]`), while both `_V_OPEN` and `_V_CLOSE` count 1 → mismatch → malformed. Correct.
  - **(c) `<doctrine>` missing `std`** — `_DOCTRINE_RE` requires `std` before `ref` in that order, so `<doctrine ref="1.4">` fails to match (`doctrines=[]`), while `_D_OPEN`/`_D_CLOSE` count 1 → mismatch → malformed. Correct.
  - `strip_tags` inner-text preservation — `_ANY_TAG_RE = r'</?(?:verse|doctrine)\b[^>]*>'` matches only the tag markers themselves (name + attributes up to `>`), never touching the captured inner text, so both open and close tags are cleanly excised and the surrounding/inner prose is untouched.
- I also checked an untested but spec-relevant case — an "extra attribute" tag like `<verse ref="x" foo="bar">text</verse>` — and confirmed the same open/close-count mismatch logic catches it as malformed (the strict regex won't match past `ref="x"` if another attribute follows), consistent with the brief's "missing/extra attribute" wording.

## Issues

**Minor**
- `content_bank/lib/citation_tags.py:90-91` — `_DOCTRINE_RE` requires attributes in the exact order `std` then `ref`. A well-formed doctrine tag with attributes reversed (`<doctrine ref="1.4" std="WCF">`) will be treated as malformed. This matches the one example format shown in the module docstring and the brief, so it's not a spec violation, but it's an implicit assumption worth a one-line comment noting attribute order is significant (or acceptance that this is intentionally strict).
- No test exercises the "extra attribute" malformed case mentioned in the brief's `malformed` description, even though the code correctly handles it (verified by hand above). Coverage gap only, not a correctness defect.

No Critical or Important issues found.

## Task Quality Verdict: Approved
